findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The floor of the walk-in freezer has an accumulation of chunks of ice and debris on it. 
2. The floor under and around the soda syrups across from the walk-in cooler has an accumulation of debris and soda syrup residue on it. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are cleaned and maintained clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The cooler containing salads and dressings in the drive-through was observed to be at an ambient temperature of 60F. CORRECTED- These items had been in there approximately for two hours and were immediately moved to another cooler. The owner stated that these will be served and gone before lunch is over (putting it within the four hour time frame allotted for Time as Control). The owner stated that they will be calling an electrician due to the breaker that the cooler is plugged into has flipped twice now and turned off the cooler. The breaker was flipped again and the cooler dropped to under 41F. The inspector instructed the owner to reach out when the issue has been fixed to spot check it. If the inspector is not reached out to, the inspector will spot check it before the next routine inspection. Ensure that TCS food items are held at 41F or under.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was not an employee who is a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) in the facility. The inspector discussed with the PIC to have multiple employees who are CFPMs to ensure there is always at least one on duty during all hours of operation. Ensure that there is at least one employee who is food manager certified present at the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The sealing around the handwashing sink next to the tea station and the preparation sink in the kitchen is observed to be in disrepair. Ensure that this sealing is replaced and made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: None of the employees working at the time of the inspection were certified food protection managers. PIC mentioned that two more employees are in the process of getting food manager certified. Ensure that there is at least one employee who is food manager certified present at the facility all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: There was a significant amount of ice build-up on the shelves stored in the walk in freezer. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure to maintain non-food contact surfaces of equipment as frequent as necessary to prevent ice build-up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There was a leak observed at the faucet handles of the produce washing sink. PIC mentioned that a work order will be placed as soon as possible. Ensure that faucets are maintained in good repair and are in leak free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand washing sink between cooked and raw is not functioning properly. The hand sink is marked out of order. Plumber has been called and will correct the sink Monday morning. Ensure that employees are moving to the hand sink by the 3 part sink or properly wash hands as needed. A follow up will be conducted on 4/2/24. If the sink is not fixed by Tuesday for the follow up inspection, please call and let the inspector know.  

5-203.11: (A) Specified under LAW, facility must have a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES. (B) If APPROVED, automatic handwashing may be substituted. (C) IF APPROVED, chemically treated towelettes can be used.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee jacket to be stuffed between boxes of single use items. Make sure to have employees store personal items properly. The jacket was moved to the back on the hooks provided. 

6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the sani bucket by the front (near cashier area) hand washing station to be low on quaternary ammonium - 100 ppm. Ensure frequent changes of sanitization buckets in order to maintain appropriate concentrations - 200 to 400 ppm. Discussed with employee. Employee went to remake the sanitization buckets with quaternary ammonium from the 3 compartment sink. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed dust on the small fan plugged into and on top of the prep area in the kitchen. Fan should be cleaned of dust and debris. Observed dust on walk-in cooler fans. Wash, rinse, sanitize as needed. Discussed with PIC.
